candidates.description: StubHub CEO Eric Baker built his company's reputation on being a neutral marketplace for fans, but SEC filings just revealed he also runs a hedge fund that bankrolls the same scalpers who dominate his platform. A class-action lawsuit filed this week accuses Baker and StubHub of deceptive practices after thousands of World Cup ticket holders were left stranded outside stadiums with tickets that never existed. We break down how a ticket bought for $100 can net a scalper 400% to 1,000% profit, and why StubHub might be less referee than player. One bar in Brooklyn sold 900 tickets at $10 each just to watch a season finale on a big screen, and there's now a dedicated Kalshi market for whether two contestants will couple up.
